nodes.summary: Let $k, b \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $f$ assign a Boolean value to each wire $x \in \mathbb{N}$, with Booleans ordered by $\mathrm{false} < \mathrm{true}$. If the sequence $f(b), f(b + 1), \dots, f(b + 2^k - 1)$ is bitonic, then running the bitonic merger on the block $[b, b + 2^k)$ on $f$ gives an assignment $g$ that is sorted on that block: $g(b + i) \le g(b + j)$ whenever $i \le j < 2^k$.
nodes.title: The bitonic merger sorts every bitonic `0`-`1` input

nodes.summary: The bitonic merger on the block of wires $[b, b + 2^k)$ is the list of comparators defined by recursion on $k$. For $k = 0$ it is empty. On the block $[b, b + 2^{k+1})$ it is the half-cleaner on $[b, b + 2^{k+1})$, followed by the bitonic merger on $[b, b + 2^k)$, followed by the bitonic merger on $[b + 2^k, b + 2^{k+1})$.
nodes.title: Bitonic merger

nodes.summary: Let $k, b \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $f$ assign a Boolean value to each wire $x \in \mathbb{N}$, with Booleans ordered by $\mathrm{false} < \mathrm{true}$. Running Batcher's bitonic sorter on the block $[b, b + 2^k)$ on $f$ gives an assignment $g$ that is sorted on that block: $g(b + i) \le g(b + j)$ whenever $i \le j < 2^k$.
nodes.title: The bitonic sorter sorts every `0`-`1` input

nodes.summary: A comparator $(i, j)$ puts the minimum of the values on wires $i$ and $j$ on wire $i$ and the maximum on wire $j$. Batcher's bitonic sorter on the block of wires $[b, b + 2^k)$ is the list of comparators defined by recursion on $k$. For $k = 0$ it is empty. On the block $[b, b + 2^{k+1})$ it is Batcher's bitonic sorter on $[b, b + 2^k)$, followed by Batcher's bitonic sorter on $[b + 2^k, b + 2^{k+1})$ with every…
nodes.title: Batcher's bitonic sorter on a block of wires

nodes.summary: For every $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and every linearly ordered type $\alpha$, Batcher's bitonic sorting network on $2^k$ wires sorts inputs over $\alpha$: for every assignment $v$ of elements of $\alpha$ to the wires $0, 1, \dots, 2^k - 1$, the output of the network on $v$ is monotone in the wire order.
nodes.title: Batcher's bitonic sorter sorts every input over every linear order

nodes.summary: For $k \in \mathbb{N}$, Batcher's bitonic sorting network on $2^k$ wires is the comparator network on the wires $0, 1, \dots, 2^k - 1$ made of the comparators of Batcher's bitonic sorter on the block $[0, 2^k)$ that join two wires below $2^k$ (in fact all of them), applied in the same order.
nodes.title: Batcher's bitonic sorting network

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linear order. For wires $i, j \in \mathbb{N}$ and an assignment $f$ of values in $\alpha$ to the wires $x \in \mathbb{N}$, the comparator $(i, j)$ applied to $f$ puts $\min(f(i), f(j))$ on wire $i$, puts $\max(f(i), f(j))$ on wire $j$ when $j \ne i$, and leaves every other wire unchanged.
nodes.title: Comparator on natural-number-indexed wires

nodes.summary: Let $N \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $P$ be a list of comparators on natural-number-indexed wires, each of which joins two wires below $N$. For every Boolean input $v$ on the wires $0, \dots, N - 1$, run the network on $N$ wires obtained from $P$ on $v$ and extend its output by $\mathrm{false}$ to all wires in $\mathbb{N}$; the result equals the result of running $P$ on the extension of $v$ by $\mathrm{false}$.
nodes.title: Transported comparator lists agree with the original on Boolean inputs

nodes.summary: For $N \in \mathbb{N}$ and a Boolean vector $v = (v_0, \dots, v_{N-1})$, its extension by $\mathrm{false}$ is the function on $\mathbb{N}$ that takes the value $v_j$ at each $j < N$ and the value $\mathrm{false}$ at each $j \ge N$.
nodes.title: Extension of a Boolean vector by false

nodes.summary: Let $m \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $s_0, s_1, \dots, s_{2m-1}$ be a bitonic sequence of Booleans, ordered by $\mathrm{false} < \mathrm{true}$. For $i < m$ put $\ell_i = \min(s_i, s_{i+m})$ and $u_i = \max(s_i, s_{i+m})$. Then either $\ell_i = \mathrm{false}$ for every $i < m$ and $u_0, \dots, u_{m-1}$ is bitonic, or $u_i = \mathrm{true}$ for every $i < m$ and $\ell_0, \dots, \ell_{m-1}$ is bitonic.
nodes.title: The half-cleaner lemma

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $m$ and $b$, the half-cleaner on the block of wires $[b, b + 2m)$ is the list of comparators $(b + i, b + m + i)$ for $i = 0, 1, \dots, m - 1$, in this order: it compares wire $b + i$ with wire $b + m + i$.
nodes.title: Half-cleaner

nodes.summary: A sequence $s : \mathbb{N} \to \{0, 1\}$ is bitonic of length $L$ if either $s$ or its complement $1 - s$ is an interval indicator of length $L$; that is, on the positions $0, \dots, L - 1$ it has the form $0^a 1^b 0^c$ or $1^a 0^b 1^c$. Values of $s$ at positions $i \ge L$ are unconstrained.
nodes.title: Bitonic 0-1 sequences

nodes.summary: A sequence $s : \mathbb{N} \to \{0, 1\}$ is an interval indicator of length $L$ if there are natural numbers $a \le e \le L$ such that for every $i < L$, $s(i) = 1$ exactly when $a \le i < e$.
nodes.title: Interval indicators

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $k$ and $b$, the bitonic merger on the block of wires $[b, b + 2^k)$ has $k \cdot 2^{k-1}$ comparators; precisely, twice its number of comparators equals $k \cdot 2^k$.
nodes.title: Size of the bitonic merger

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $k$ and $b$, the bitonic sorter on the block of $\mathbb{N}$-indexed wires $[b, b + 2^k)$ has $k(k+1)2^k/4$ comparators; precisely, four times its number of comparators equals $k(k+1)2^k$.
nodes.title: Size of the bitonic sorter on a block of wires

nodes.summary: For every natural number $k$, Batcher's bitonic sorting network on $2^k$ wires has $k(k+1)2^k/4$ comparators; precisely, four times its number of comparators equals $k(k+1)2^k$.
nodes.title: Comparator count of Batcher's bitonic sorter

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $m$ and $b$, the half-cleaner on the block of wires $[b, b + 2m)$ has exactly $m$ comparators.
nodes.title: Size of the half-cleaner

nodes.summary: For a natural number $N$ and a list of comparators on wires indexed by $\mathbb{N}$, this is the network on the $N$ wires $0, \dots, N - 1$ that keeps, in their original order, the comparators $(i, j)$ with $i < N$ and $j < N$, and drops all the others.
nodes.title: Restricting comparators to finitely many wires

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linear order, let $l, h \in \mathbb{N}$, and let $c$ be a list of comparators on $\mathbb{N}$-indexed wires each of which joins two wires $x$ with $l \le x < h$. If an input $f : \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$ takes the same value $a$ on every wire $x$ with $l \le x < h$, then running $c$ on $f$ gives an output that also takes the value $a$ on every such wire.
nodes.title: Constant blocks stay constant

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linear order, let $m, b \in \mathbb{N}$, and let $f : \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$ be an input on $\mathbb{N}$-indexed wires. Running the half-cleaner on $[b, b + 2m)$ on $f$ puts $\min(f(b + i), f(b + m + i))$ on wire $b + i$ and $\max(f(b + i), f(b + m + i))$ on wire $b + m + i$ for every $i < m$, and leaves the value $f(x)$ on every wire $x$ outside $[b, b + 2m)$ unchanged.
nodes.title: Output of the half-cleaner

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linear order and let $ps$ be a list of comparators $(i, j)$ on $\mathbb{N}$-indexed wires that all lie within $[l, h)$, that is, $l \le i < h$ and $l \le j < h$ for every $(i, j)$ in $ps$. Then for every input $f : \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$ and every wire $x$ with $x < l$ or $h \le x$, the value of wire $x$ after running $ps$ on $f$ is $f(x)$.
nodes.title: Locality of comparator networks

nodes.summary: Let $ps$ be a list of comparators on $\mathbb{N}$-indexed wires and let $ps'$ be obtained by replacing each comparator $(i, j)$ in $ps$ by $(j, i)$. For every input $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathrm{Bool}$ and every wire $x$, the value of wire $x$ after running $ps'$ on $f$ is the negation of the value of wire $x$ after running $ps$ on the complemented input $y \mapsto \lnot f(y)$.
nodes.title: Reversing the comparators conjugates the network by complement on Booleans

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linear order. Given a list $ps$ of comparators, each a pair $(i, j)$ of natural numbers, and an input $f : \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$ giving the value on each wire, running $ps$ on $f$ applies the comparators of $ps$ to the wire values one after another, from first to last. The comparator $(i, j)$ puts the minimum of the values on wires $i$ and $j$ on wire $i$ and their maximum on wire $j$, and leaves…
nodes.title: Running a comparator network on natural-number-indexed wires

nodes.summary: A Boolean sequence $g : \mathbb{N} \to \mathrm{Bool}$ is sorted on the block $[b, b + L)$ if $g(b + i) \le g(b + j)$ for all $i \le j < L$, where Booleans are ordered by $\mathrm{false} < \mathrm{true}$.
nodes.title: Sorted on a block

nodes.summary: A list $ps$ of comparators, each a pair $(i, j)$ of natural numbers, lies within $[l, h)$ if every comparator $(i, j)$ in $ps$ satisfies $l \le i < h$ and $l \le j < h$.
nodes.title: Comparators within an interval

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
